title: 1. The site loads: home page with navigation
proves: The React/Vite storefront is up and talking to the FastAPI backend: the nav links (Home, Products, About Us, Log In, Create Account) render, and the featured products are loaded from the API.

title: 2. Products page lists the whole catalogue as cards
proves: All 102 rows of the catalogue table appear as product cards (image, name, price, one-liner), fed by GET /api/products.

title: 3. The seeded test user can log in
proves: Logging in as test@campuscustoms.yale.edu with the provided password succeeds (the nav greets “Hi, Test!”), so the seeded PBKDF2 hash verifies against the backend.

title: 4. Chat checks inventory: exact stock and price from the database
proves: Asked about size M of the Yale Grandpa Hoodie, the chat answered with 25 in stock at $68, exactly the values in the inventory and catalogue tables.
details: How many Yale Grandpa Hoodies do you have in size M, and what's the price?
The Yale Grandpa Hoodie has 25 in size M, and it’s $68. Boola boola! 🎃

title: 5. Chat says definitively when a size is out of stock
proves: Size L has quantity 0 in the database, and the chat states plainly that it is out of stock (no hedging), then offers the sizes that are in stock.
details: Is the Yale Grandpa Hoodie available in size L?
Size L is out of stock for the Yale Grandpa Hoodie. It’s available in XS, S, M, XL, and XXL.

title: 6. A category question (“What hoodies do you have?”) returns dynamic product cards
proves: The agent searched the catalogue and the site rendered 12 hoodie cards in the “Chat picks” strip (and in the chat). Every card's category is Hoodies and every price matches the database.
details: We have 27 hoodies in total, and I’ve pulled up 12 options below to browse. Boola boola! 🎃

title: 7. Clicking a chat-surfaced card opens the full product page
proves: The first chat card opened /products/basic-hoodie-big-yale with the large image, full description, price, sizes and stock, the same single-item page as the Products grid.

title: 8. Problem 9 usability feature: SKU info on the product page
proves: Picking size M shows SKU CC-0507-M with its stock count and a Copy SKU button. The SKU is built from that size's permanent inventory-table id, so staff and shoppers can name the exact unit.

title: 9. Problem 9 usability feature: chat history reloads with a welcome-back recap
proves: After logging out and back in, the test user's earlier conversation (including checks 4–6) reloads from the database, ending with a recap of the products they looked at, re-priced from live stock.
details:
